title: Thought the accelerator taught growth hacking, but discovered subtraction to a single thing
dek: The hardest part of subtraction isn't cutting entertainment—it's eliminating the second-most important thing to obsess over the most important one.
why: This episode explains how founders use singular focus and ritual to transform scattered teams into growth machines, skipping technical details.
who: Founders and team leads wanting to understand high-pressure accelerators like HF0, or designing internal sprint structures.
skip: If you're not interested in AI music generation details, you can skip the Suno competition section after the 44-minute mark.

points.h: HF0's selectivity with ten companies per batch beats Y Combinator's scale
points.body: HF0 takes ten companies per batch, three times yearly; Y Combinator takes two hundred per batch, four times yearly. Guo Jing (郭靖) calls Y Combinator ‘spray and pray’—casting wide nets and betting on probability to produce winners. Early-stage accelerators theoretically have lower success rates, so they need larger pools to hedge risk; HF0 does the opposite, shrinking the denominator to its minimum and compensating only through extreme selectivity, making its acceptance rate far lower than Y Combinator's.

points.h: OpenRouter made barely enough for coffee, and that was the whole strategy
points.body: At HF0's weekly Monday Demo Dinners, each company reports progress on a single metric. OpenRouter didn't report revenue, but weekly token calls—founder Louis often said the company's earnings barely covered two cups of coffee. Months later, Stripe acquired OpenRouter for 7 billion dollars, and HF0 co-founder Evan posted to the alumni group with the caption ‘enough for coffee’.

points.h: Jumping from 100 to 150 daily outreach contacts forced growth to emerge
points.body: During his growth obsession, Guo Jing consulted growth expert Blake Anderson on influencer partnerships. Guo said he'd contacted over 100 influencers in several months; Anderson said he contacts 150 per day—the order-of-magnitude gap made Guo realize his system was broken, so he rebuilt his outreach, follow-up, and conversion flow; now his team contacts 200 influencers per day.

points.h: Price increases to drive growth collide with the conservation of energy
points.body: Guo Jing tried raising prices 30% to drive growth, but later realized this was ‘conservation of energy’—the conversion gains from raising prices are offset by potential-user churn and reputation loss. He noticed the best products like OpenAI and Anthropic don't rely on pricing tricks; annual plans are just monthly times 12 at 20% off, numbers decided casually, with real effort focused on model quality itself.

points.h: Real subtraction means cutting even the second-most important thing from focus
points.body: People think HF0's ‘subtraction’ means founders skip socializing and relaxing; Guo Jing says that's backwards—cutting entertainment is the easy part. Real subtraction is fixating only on what matters most to the company, even excluding the second-most important thing: if a major partnership moves slowly, abandon it, because trying to do everything means doing nothing about what actually matters most.

points.h: November 1 arrived and revenue doubled overnight from months of accumulated momentum
points.body: In the first half of the program, except for OpenRouter—which had already achieved flywheel effects—the whole cohort saw almost no growth, making Dave question his judgment. On October 30, everyone was still encouraging each other; on November 1, Guo Jing woke to find daily revenue had doubled—the accumulated influencer system and paid event both took effect the same day, then grew another 50%, then doubled again.

points.h: OpenRouter's moat may not survive a straightforward price war
points.body: Guo Jing observed that OpenRouter works because it executes one thing to extreme simplicity: no aggressive monetization, no reckless fundraising, just ‘a unified interface for calling all large models’. Developers don't rewrite code to switch models, and model makers rush to integrate because the call-volume leaderboard already carries authority. But Guo Jing admits this advantage might not withstand pure price competition.

points.h: AI music can master vocal technique but cannot generate imperfect emotional moments
points.body: Guo Jing says AI music can now achieve ‘vocal fusion’ humans cannot, yet cannot generate the moments that truly move—those imperfect, rawly emotional instants. He cites Li Zhi (李志)'s song captured on phone video at a Nanjing bar as more alive than the later mastered version, and Shan Yichun (山一纯)'s mid-performance crack and hesitation on The Voice of China moved him more than a perfect take would.

terms.def: Investing broadly without selectivity; batching bets and relying on probability to produce winners.
HF0 founder Dave's core principle of relentless focus on a single priority, removing everything else.
HF0's weekly Monday ritual where each company reports two-minute progress updates on a single metric.
OpenRouter's early positioning: one interface for developers to call any large model without rewriting code.

facts.k: ACE Studio monthly revenue growth during HF0

quotes.text: It's more or less a joke—the spray and pray logic. Spray means spraying water, pray means praying, you spray everything out there.
Louis used to say our revenue is just enough to buy two cups of coffee—he said it constantly.
I was like, I've contacted maybe over 100 in several months; he's like, I contact 150 per day.
Things that seem unstable become stable once you increase the scale.
Looking back now, I feel like energy is conserved: when you raise prices, you lose potential users, and those lost potential users offset your gains.
Subtraction isn't cutting unimportant leisure activities—the hard part is fixating only on what matters most to your company, even eliminating the second-most important thing.
October 30, everyone was still encouraging each other; November 1 morning I woke up and our daily revenue had doubled.
What truly moves people are those imperfect instants, those moments of genuine emotion.
